approach: Exact 23-component SRK+Peneloux classic-mixing parity; component-specific water Kij copied from the NeqSim runtime to PVTsim; licensed topology-bracketed PT flashes refined for both boundary families. The frozen baseline was retained, then an explicit clone-only branch-aware compatibility profile was screened jointly against the GO->GOW branch, OW->GOW branch, and their coupled endpoint.
conclusions: The frozen/default NeqSim model remains only partially aligned with PVTsim and is not declared interchangeable: its secondary boundary differs by about 8.8 degC. A new explicit opt-in software-compatibility profile passes the joint gates without changing the frozen payload. With water-Kij multipliers 0.98325 for GO->GOW and 0.932 for OW->GOW, the main boundary has MAE 0.735 degC (15/15 roots within 2 degC), the secondary boundary has MAE 0.299 degC (7/7 roots), and the endpoint is 228.550885 bara inside the PVTsim 228.55-228.56 bara direct-topology bracket. This is a PVTsim software compatibility mode, not an experimental fluid calibration; production/default promotion remains disallowed until exact-fluid laboratory data support it.

figure_discussion.title: Same-definition boundary overlay
figure_discussion.observation: Main curves nearly overlap over 10-228 bara, whereas secondary curves are visibly separated by about 8-9.5 C.
figure_discussion.mechanism: The secondary disappearing-gas boundary is more sensitive to component partitioning and phase-stability implementation.
figure_discussion.implication: Agreement on the main branch cannot be generalized to the full aqueous boundary network.
figure_discussion.recommendation: Use branch-specific validation and do not substitute one package for the other on the secondary branch.

figure_discussion.title: Boundary-temperature deviation
figure_discussion.observation: Main bias grows monotonically from -0.025 to -2.025 C; secondary bias is -8.10 to -9.48 C.
figure_discussion.mechanism: Systematic pressure dependence is much larger than the 0.025/0.125 C localization half-widths.
figure_discussion.implication: Additional temperature-grid refinement cannot remove the secondary discrepancy.
figure_discussion.recommendation: Compare pseudo-component parameters and stability thresholds before any Kij calibration.

figure_discussion.title: Endpoint topology audit
figure_discussion.observation: PVTsim gives GOW, then GW, then no phase-property rows around 313.415 C, then GO.
figure_discussion.mechanism: Vanishing-phase stability and critical-endpoint handling dominate near boundary termination.
figure_discussion.implication: The NeqSim endpoint is not independently closed by PVTsim.
figure_discussion.recommendation: Keep the endpoint unresolved until a dedicated PVTsim endpoint calculation succeeds.

figure_discussion.title: Licensed benchmark parity
figure_discussion.observation: All 15 main points remain near parity; all seven secondary points fall systematically below it.
figure_discussion.mechanism: The branch-specific offset indicates model-form rather than random flash-grid error.
figure_discussion.implication: Only the main boundary has engineering-level cross-package validation.
figure_discussion.recommendation: Apply separate confidence labels to each branch.

figure_discussion.title: Boundary metrology uncertainty
figure_discussion.observation: Monte Carlo MAE distributions are narrow around 0.878 C and 8.819 C.
figure_discussion.mechanism: Licensed bracket widths are far smaller than the software-to-software difference.
figure_discussion.implication: Numerical localization does not explain the secondary mismatch.
figure_discussion.recommendation: Stop refining the temperature grid and focus on model-form diagnostics.

figure_discussion.title: Uncertainty driver ranking
figure_discussion.observation: Secondary model gap dominates numerical half-step effects by two orders of magnitude.
figure_discussion.mechanism: Both packages are converged; their stability and property implementations differ.
figure_discussion.implication: Further grid densification has low decision value.
figure_discussion.recommendation: Prioritize parameter/stability audits and experimental calibration.

figure_discussion.title: Secondary fit versus mainline preservation
figure_discussion.observation: Multiplying all water Kij values by 0.932 reduces the seven-point secondary MAE from 8.819 C to 0.292 C, but the ordinary main branch is absent by 226 bara.
figure_discussion.mechanism: Water-hydrocarbon binary interactions influence both disappearing-gas and disappearing-water stability conditions, so a constant correction moves more than the target branch.
figure_discussion.implication: Cross-package equality on the secondary branch cannot be treated as a valid calibration when it changes the already verified mainline topology.
figure_discussion.recommendation: Keep the frozen baseline; use laboratory three-phase data and a targeted stability-model investigation before considering physical calibration.

figure_discussion.title: Endpoint pressure refinement
figure_discussion.observation: PVTsim retains a direct GOW-to-GO transition at 228.5 bara, while 228.6 bara already contains an unresolved flash interval; higher pressures develop GW and a wider error wedge.
figure_discussion.mechanism: Vanishing-phase stability and near-critical root handling change the observed phase path at the branch termination.
figure_discussion.implication: Direct-topology termination is bracketed to 228.5-228.6 bara, but this ordinary PT scan does not establish a PVTsim critical endpoint.
figure_discussion.recommendation: Use 228 bara as the cross-package operational limit and keep the endpoint package-dependent until a dedicated critical calculation or laboratory data closes it.

figure_discussion.title: Secondary-root thermodynamic diagnostics
figure_discussion.observation: All seven formal roots pass the 1e-7 residual gate; at 284-286 bara a lower root cluster has gas-oil L1 distances from 9.5e-5 to 3.2e-3 and includes a 286 bara / 249.375 C critical endpoint.
figure_discussion.mechanism: The fixed-pressure zero-TPD equations contain both a distinct disappearing-gas branch and a separate near-coalescent oil-gas network.
figure_discussion.implication: A converged root can belong to the wrong physical network; package-to-package temperature proximity is not a valid branch selector.
figure_discussion.recommendation: Preserve root identity, global-stability evidence, phase distance and pressure continuity in every boundary result.

figure_discussion.title: Full workflow-candidate validation
figure_discussion.observation: Fresh recalculation reproduces 15/15 main roots within 2.3e-13 C, 7/7 secondary roots within 3.2e-6 C, and the endpoint within 4e-11 bara.
figure_discussion.mechanism: The accepted candidate changes only root-network reporting; the frozen SRK/classic physical model is byte-for-byte unchanged.
figure_discussion.implication: The mainline remains fully operational while the 8.819 C secondary package gap persists as model-form uncertainty.
figure_discussion.recommendation: Deploy the reporting/test improvement but do not promote a Kij or pure-component calibration without exact-fluid laboratory data.

figure_discussion.title: Supplemental same-definition envelope comparison
figure_discussion.observation: The 15-point main boundary stays closely overlaid, whereas all seven refined secondary points place PVTsim 8.133-9.542 C below NeqSim.
figure_discussion.mechanism: The separation is confined to the water-rich disappearing-gas branch and is therefore consistent with package-dependent aqueous-phase equilibrium and branch-tracking behavior, not grid localization.
figure_discussion.implication: Main-boundary use remains supported, but high-pressure secondary boundary temperatures cannot be transferred between the packages.
figure_discussion.recommendation: Keep the frozen mainline and label the secondary branch as package-dependent until same-fluid experimental data are obtained.

figure_discussion.title: Refined secondary-boundary deviation
figure_discussion.observation: The deviation is monotonic from -8.133 C at 284 bara to -9.542 C at 300 bara; no point enters the +/-2 C comparison band.
figure_discussion.mechanism: The smooth pressure trend and 0.025-0.125 C transition brackets show that the difference is systematic model form or branch selection, rather than flash-grid resolution.
figure_discussion.implication: Reducing grid spacing cannot close the secondary-boundary gap.
figure_discussion.recommendation: Use the refined values as regression benchmarks only; do not calibrate Kij or pure-component parameters without experimental evidence.

figure_discussion.title: Endpoint topology and unresolved-output band
figure_discussion.observation: Direct PVTsim GOW-to-GO topology persists through 228.55 bara and is no longer direct at 228.56 bara. Across the complete campaign, 4,569 solver-successful numeric outputs omit phase identity.
figure_discussion.mechanism: Above the termination bracket an intervening GW region and an output band without phase labels interrupt direct branch continuation.
figure_discussion.implication: The scan can localize topology termination but cannot claim a solved PVTsim critical endpoint or safely infer the missing phase labels.
figure_discussion.recommendation: Retain unresolved rows verbatim, preserve the NeqSim endpoint as a package-specific result, and seek explicit phase/stability output or same-fluid experiments before endpoint calibration.

figure_discussion.title: Branch-aware compatibility envelope
figure_discussion.observation: The opt-in profile preserves all 15 main roots and all seven secondary roots. Its coupled endpoint is 228.550885 bara, inside the direct PVTsim topology bracket of 228.55-228.56 bara.
figure_discussion.mechanism: Each physical boundary family receives its own water-interaction scaling on a cloned working fluid. This avoids the topology loss caused by applying the secondary-branch correction globally to the main branch.
figure_discussion.implication: PVTsim-compatible boundary calculations can now be requested explicitly without modifying the verified default NeqSim payload or silently mixing boundary definitions.
figure_discussion.recommendation: Keep the profile opt-in and require the caller to select GO_TO_GOW or OW_TO_GOW explicitly; retain the frozen model as the operational default.

figure_discussion.title: Deviation reduction without default-model regression
figure_discussion.observation: Main-boundary MAE is 0.735 degC with a 1.669 degC maximum, while secondary-boundary MAE falls from about 8.8 degC in the frozen model to 0.299 degC with a 0.590 degC maximum.
figure_discussion.mechanism: The two fitted multipliers address different sensitivity regimes of the main hydrocarbon-rich boundary and the high-pressure water-rich boundary instead of forcing one global parameter to serve both.
figure_discussion.implication: The software comparison target is achieved across the declared pressure ranges, but the fitted factors remain package-compatibility settings rather than evidence of improved physical truth.
figure_discussion.recommendation: Use the profile for controlled PVTsim reproduction and regression testing; do not promote it to the default physical model until exact-fluid phase boundary measurements are available.
